question: What would a TV ad campaign for Punctual Pros look like?
html:
Punctual Pros TV Campaign

Punctual Pros would run zip-targeted connected TV (CTV) that sells each brand's existing on-time promise. The CTV would be measured by booked jobs against holdout zips, not by viewing metrics (Punctual Pros ad plan).

The message

  • The ads reuse the brands' existing promises instead of inventing new claims (Punctual Pros ad plan):
  • One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
  • Ben Franklin: the $5-a-minute guarantee.
  • Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician."
  • Two creatives are in test: "Storm Ready" (:15) and "We Watch the Clock" (:30, cut to :15).

How the buy works

  • Self-serve CTV now has minimums of $50 to $500 and CPMs of roughly $15 to $40, with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • That lets a portfolio company of about $22M buy TV only in its ~240 zips. It avoids paying for the full Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.
  • Candidate vendors are Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads and YouTube on TV screens. Vibe quotes $15 to $35 CPMs and reaches Hulu, Paramount+, Peacock, Disney+, Tubi, Pluto and Roku.
  • Spots run at :15 or :30 in 1920x1080 at about -24 LKFS loudness.
  • Frequency is capped at 3 per week.

The role TV plays

  • CTV builds familiarity before the furnace fails. It should then lift branded search and Google Local Services Ads (LSA) conversion.
  • LSA remains the always-on base, at $39 to $57 per lead and a ~44% book rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Completion rate is not a success measure. It runs ~94 to 99% by construction.

Test sequence

WeekCTV focusTotal weekly test budget (all channels)
1Tracking numbers, pixels, 15% of Tier-I zips held out$8,000
2Creative A/B, 50/50 by zip cluster$12,500
3Frequency check$12,500
4Booked jobs per 10k housing units, exposed vs holdout; shift 20% to winner$12,500
5Weather triggers in alternating counties$12,500
6Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney or YouTubenot shown

The CTV share of each weekly budget is not broken out in the plan (Punctual Pros ad plan).

What is still unknown

  • No public home-services benchmark exists for CTV cost per site visit or cost per lead.
  • The plan's $12 cost per visit is an assumption (est.) drawn from direct-to-consumer case studies. The week-8 read must replace it.
  • Season-long CTV spend and the target cost per booked job are not in the plan. Defining them requires ServiceTitan job data by zip and source, plus franchisee margin by trade.

Next actions

  • Confirm that ServiceTitan tracking numbers, QR codes and the Tier-I zip holdouts are live before any CTV impressions run.
  • Brief production on the two :15 cuts against the delivery specs listed above.
  • Set the week-4 decision rule now, so the 20% budget shift is not judged on completion rate.
  • Set a target cost per booked job by trade, so the week-8 read can replace the $12 assumption.

# Punctual Pros TV Campaign

Punctual Pros would run zip-targeted connected TV (CTV) that sells each brand's existing on-time promise. The CTV would be measured by booked jobs against holdout zips, not by viewing metrics (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## The message

- The ads reuse the brands' existing promises instead of inventing new claims (Punctual Pros ad plan):
  - One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
  - Ben Franklin: the $5-a-minute guarantee.
  - Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician."
- Two creatives are in test: "Storm Ready" (:15) and "We Watch the Clock" (:30, cut to :15).

## How the buy works

- Self-serve CTV now has minimums of $50 to $500 and CPMs of roughly $15 to $40, with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- That lets a portfolio company of about $22M buy TV only in its ~240 zips. It avoids paying for the full Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA.
- Candidate vendors are Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads and YouTube on TV screens. Vibe quotes $15 to $35 CPMs and reaches Hulu, Paramount+, Peacock, Disney+, Tubi, Pluto and Roku.
- Spots run at :15 or :30 in 1920x1080 at about -24 LKFS loudness.
- Frequency is capped at 3 per week.

## The role TV plays

- CTV builds familiarity before the furnace fails. It should then lift branded search and Google Local Services Ads (LSA) conversion.
- LSA remains the always-on base, at $39 to $57 per lead and a ~44% book rate (Punctual Pros ad plan).
- Completion rate is not a success measure. It runs ~94 to 99% by construction.

## Test sequence

| Week | CTV focus | Total weekly test budget (all channels) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tracking numbers, pixels, 15% of Tier-I zips held out | $8,000 |
| 2 | Creative A/B, 50/50 by zip cluster | $12,500 |
| 3 | Frequency check | $12,500 |
| 4 | Booked jobs per 10k housing units, exposed vs holdout; shift 20% to winner | $12,500 |
| 5 | Weather triggers in alternating counties | $12,500 |
| 6 | Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney or YouTube | not shown |

The CTV share of each weekly budget is not broken out in the plan (Punctual Pros ad plan).

## What is still unknown

- No public home-services benchmark exists for CTV cost per site visit or cost per lead.
- The plan's $12 cost per visit is an assumption (est.) drawn from direct-to-consumer case studies. The week-8 read must replace it.
- Season-long CTV spend and the target cost per booked job are not in the plan. Defining them requires ServiceTitan job data by zip and source, plus franchisee margin by trade.

## Next actions

- Confirm that ServiceTitan tracking numbers, QR codes and the Tier-I zip holdouts are live before any CTV impressions run.
- Brief production on the two :15 cuts against the delivery specs listed above.
- Set the week-4 decision rule now, so the 20% budget shift is not judged on completion rate.
- Set a target cost per booked job by trade, so the week-8 read can replace the $12 assumption.
